text: Amidst conflicting information about
the international situation, what you
need is a sober and objective
perspective. That is what we always
strive to provide. Following are the
notable developments. Ladies and
gentlemen, European Commission
President Ursula von der Leyen affirmed
that the EU continues to support
Ukraine after U.S. President Donald
Trump suggested that Kyiv needs a new
leader. She also announced that the
European Union will provide additional
funding to purchase missiles and
unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for
Ukraine. According to the Russian news
agency TASS, following a phone call
with Ukrainian President Volodymyr
Zelensky, von der Leyen stated on
October 12 that the EU will allocate
more funds for missiles and UAVs to
strengthen Ukraine's defense
capabilities and protect its airspace.
On the social network X, she wrote, "I
expressed my solidarity with the people
of Ukraine and my full support for Mr.
Zelensky." She stated that Ukraine will
be one of the key topics of discussion
at the European Council this week. In
it, EU leaders will review Kyiv's
financial needs for the coming year and
measures to mobilize further
international support. The EC President
also affirmed that the EU will soon
open two more negotiation chapters with
Ukraine, while emphasizing that this
process is achieving substantive
progress. Previously, President Trump
publicly suggested that Ukraine seek a
new leader capable of reaching a deal
to end the conflict with Russia.
Speaking at the White House on October
10, he argued that Mr. Zelensky had
repeatedly missed opportunities to
reach an agreement. According to AFP,
AP, and Reuters, Mr. Trump said, "I
suggest they find a new leader who can
reach a deal," while arguing that Mr.
Zelensky for some reason has been
unable to do so. The U.S. leader also
claimed that Ukraine has lost 30%of its
territory under Mr. Zelensky's
leadership, while offering assessments
on the death toll in the conflict. He
emphasized that this is a war that
should never have happened and
suggested that it is time for Ukraine
to have a new president. Meanwhile,
Kremlin press secretary Dmitry Peskov
stated that Moscow wishes to achieve a
comprehensive solution to the conflict
in Ukraine, aiming for a long-term
agreement that could last for decades.
Tensions regarding military support for
Ukraine have also drawn attention
following a Financial Times report on
the possibility of the US pressuring
Kyiv and European countries. Citing
unnamed European officials, the
Financial Times reported that US
officials contacted European capitals
and Kyiv on October 10 and 11. They
warned that they could stop sharing
intelligence and block US weapon
procurement programs for Ukraine.
According to these sources, this move
is related to attacks targeting
Russia's energy infrastructure. An
official cited said that the US had
contacted Kyiv and many European
countries. Among those who received
communication was Pavel Palisa, deputy
head of the Ukrainian presidential
office. However, the Financial Times
noted that the White House declined to
confirm or comment on these exchanges.
The program for Ukraine's priority list
of US weapon procurement requests was
one of the mechanisms mentioned. In the
Financial Times report, prior to
October 11, Mr. Trump wrote on Truth
Social that Russia and Ukraine had
agreed not to attack each other's
energy facilities. According to TASS,
Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov
stated that the October 9 phone call
between Russian President Vladimir
Putin and his US counterpart Donald
Trump was extremely positive, as the
two leaders discussed many topics, from
the Ukraine conflict to ice hockey. Mr.
Ushakov said the phone call lasted
about 90 minutes in a very friendly
atmosphere. President Trump wished
President Putin a happy birthday at the
very beginning, while also conveying
regards from First Lady Melania. The
two leaders exchanged a great deal, and
neither wanted to be the one to hang up
first. I hope President Trump will not
be displeased if I quote him saying he
is ready to continue talking with
President Putin today, tonight, this
evening, and even the next day. During
the phone call, Mr. Putin said that
Moscow would reconsider the timing for
resuming negotiations after the Russian
State Duma elections. In addition, the
master of the Kremlin detailed Russia's
response to Ukraine's attacks.
President Putin informed President
Trump about the situation along the
front lines and Moscow's response to
what Russia calls terrorist attacks by
Ukraine on infrastructure and civilian
targets deep within Russian territory.
The Russian leader emphasized that
Moscow maintains the initiative and
remains steadfast in its goals, while
expressing readiness to seek a
long-term diplomatic solution. However,
President Putin argued that Kyiv has
effectively sabotaged plans to
immediately resume trilateral
negotiations between Russia, Ukraine,
and the US. Mr. Ushakov said the
president thanked Mrs. Melania for her
contributions to reuniting children
with their families in Russia and
Ukraine. Russian Human Rights
Commissioner Yana Lantratova will
continue to maintain regular contact
with Mrs. Melania's team. Furthermore,
special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared
Kushner also expressed their desire to
meet with the president soon. President
Putin appreciated the interest the US
leadership has shown in dialogue with
Russia, despite their domestic agenda
and Washington's involvement in Middle
Eastern issues. However, Mr. Putin and
Mr. Trump did not specifically discuss
a direct meeting in the near future.
Regarding the Iran issue, President
Putin affirmed to the US side that
Moscow's proposal to transfer Tehran's
enriched uranium to Russia remains
valid. Mr. Ushakov reported. According
to Mr. Ushakov, President Putin noted
that Washington and Tehran maintain
indirect contacts through Qatar,
despite the confrontational rhetoric
between the two sides. Beyond global
issues, the two leaders also discussed
hockey, with President Trump praising
the achievements of Russian athlete
Alexander Ovechkin. Ukrainian President
Volodymyr Zelensky has criticized his
American counterpart Donald Trump for
his decision to lift sanctions.
Regarding Russia's oil exports, he
accused Washington of reaching a deal
with Moscow behind Kyiv's back.
According to The Guardian and RT,
Zelensky described this move as
completely unfair, entirely unlike the
way partners should behave, and a weak
decision from powerful partners. This
statement came just as Ukrainian
negotiators and European countries
supporting Kyiv were meeting with US
officials in Miami to discuss a
potential peace deal. In a voice
message sent to Western journalists on
October 9, Zelensky alleged that Trump
had used Ukrainian negotiators as a
front while pursuing a separate deal
with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
You know, this is like a happy birthday
gift for Mr. Putin. It is truly
terrible. Zelensky told Aus news in a
private phone interview, referring to
the Russian leader's 74th birthday
earlier this week. At first, Trump
ignored reporters 'questions about
Zelensky calling his decision weak.
However, the US President later
dismissed the criticism and defended
the deal, claiming it was a necessary
measure to cool down surging fuel
prices. Trump said, "We need oil for
the world, and this is the diesel that
we need." So, we are very happy to have
this supply. A US source revealed that
European governments have privately
expressed complaints about soaring
energy prices and other economic
consequences caused by the
Russia-Ukraine conflict. This source
also mentioned that there is growing
concern among the public that
hostilities will drag on for another
winter. Previously, Trump announced
that after a successful discussion with
Russian President Putin, Moscow agreed
to immediately provide over 300,000
tons of diesel to the US and global
markets. Russia will continue to supply
500,000 tons in November, an additional
1 million tons shortly after, and could
potentially add 3 million more
depending on refinery capacity. Trump
has repeatedly blamed Kyiv and Zelensky
personally for exacerbating the global
fuel crisis. He accused Ukraine of
deliberately destroying Russian
refining capacity, driving up fuel
prices for American consumers. During
his visit to Iceland last month, Mr.
Trump directly asked Mr. Zelensky to
end these attacks. Earlier this week,
Mr. Trump continued to emphasize that
the main reason for the spike in fuel
prices in the US is not the disruption
of oil shipments through the H1 Strait,
but rather Ukraine's attacks on Russian
oil refineries. US Treasury Secretary
Scott Ben also linked these attacks to
a widespread energy shock. Ladies and
gentlemen, the US has announced a
meeting with representatives from
Ukraine and European countries in Miami
on October 9 and 10 to exchange new
ideas and proposals to promote the
peace negotiation process. In the
context of the Russia-Ukraine conflict
showing no signs of cooling down, the
US announced it would host a meeting
with representatives from Ukraine and
European nations in Miami, Florida, on
October 9 and 10 to discuss new ideas
and proposals to advance peace talks.
According to sources, President Donald
Trump's special envoys Steve WC and
Chari Krisner will work with the
Ukrainian delegation, while also
inviting national security advisors
from the UK, France, Germany, along
with representatives from NATO and the
EU to attend. Ukrainian President
Vladimir Zelensky confirmed that his
country's delegation will participate
in the meeting. The discussion is
expected to focus on proposals to end
the conflict, security guarantees for
Ukraine, and plans for post-conflict
economic recovery and development.
According to the US side, the new ideas
were formed based on exchanges between
US negotiators and representatives from
Russia and Ukraine during recent trips.
Washington hopes this expanded meeting
will help the parties narrow their
differences, working toward building a
common proposal for the peace process.
Meanwhile, Kremlin spokesman Dimitri
Pescope said on October 8 that Russia
agrees with the assessment of US
Secretary of State Marbio that the
conflict in Ukraine is currently at a
stalemate. Speaking on the sidelines of
the CIS summit in Turkmenistan, Mr.
Prescope emphasized that finding a
peaceful solution will depend on
diplomatic efforts. President Zelensky
stated that the US wishes to push for a
new round of negotiations between
Russia and Ukraine in October. Moscow
has also mentioned the possibility of
holding trilateral negotiations this
month. However, the peace process has
yet to achieve significant
breakthroughs due to disagreements
between the parties over conditions to
end the conflict. The meeting in Miami
is expected to create further
opportunities to promote dialogue as
parties continue seeking solutions to
reduce tensions and move toward a
sustainable peace agreement. Speaking
at a press conference in Lisbon on
October 8, U.S. Secretary of State
Marcubio assessed that the war is
currently at a stalemate. He emphasized
that Washington wants to prevent the
fighting from escalating in the coming
month and find ways to end the conflict
. Mr. WC and Mr. Chrisner traveled to
Moscow and Kyiv at the beginning of
September. Since then, the two envoys
have continued working with the Russian
and Ukrainian sides to refine the peace
initiative. Previously, the two envoys
met with President Trump on October 8
to present the latest proposals and
receive his feedback. According to a
U.S. official, Treasury Secretary Scott
Bon and Deputy National Security
Advisor My Netham also attended the
meeting.
Keeping a clear head amidst the flow of
international information is not easy,
and we always strive to accompany you
in that endeavor. Thank you for your
attention and interest. Goodbye and see
you again.
